reading.body:
The Business Roundtable's AI lobbying is carried by a small core of lobbyists who appear on nearly every filing, not by a broad roster.

Seventeen AI filings name the same nine lobbyists, including Toula Nicole Vasilaros, Kristen Silverberg, Paul Jackson, Joshua Bolten, Matthew Spikes, Sarah Linden, Javier Gamboa, Matthew Miller and Andrew Beilein. Two more, Amy Shuart Gingrich and Casey Nelson, appear on fourteen. The remaining fifteen named lobbyists appear on eleven filings or fewer, and eight of them on just one. The pattern is a standing team that handles the AI portfolio, with occasional specialists pulled in.

The filings name two bills, HR 633 and S 146, both tied to 2025 or later. That is the entire legislative footprint the data records. It does not say what the Business Roundtable argued, what provisions it sought, or whether the bills concern model regulation, procurement, or something else. A filing reports that a client lobbied on an issue, not the position taken.

Nothing here connects to compute, buildings, or power. These are disclosure records about who lobbied and on which bills, and they carry no information about data centers, electricity demand, or the physical constraints on AI scaling. The data covers one client, one registrant, and two bills, and it should be read as a roster and a bill list rather than a measure of influence or spending.

summary: THE BUSINESS ROUNDTABLE, INC. filed 17 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI held by this site. Its clients, the lobbyists named on those filings and the AI bills they name are below. LDA registrant id 7543.
